offline memory consolidation facilitates cross-modal category learning, with time-dependent consolidation showing more beneficial effects than sleep-dependent consolidation.
time- but not sleep- dependent consolidation facilitates conceptual category formation.
time-dependent consolidation, but not sleep-dependent, facilitates the emergence of cross-modally represented concepts.

how we learn and represent knowledge about the world.
how we learn about the world around us and how we bring meaning to our environment.
the formation of conceptual knowledge and how it evolves over time, rather then with how concepts are stored in memory.

sleep does not facilitate the formation of conceptual knowledge.

the consolidation process is crucial to the formation of conceptual knowledge, but the nature of the consolidation process is not.

the formation of conceptual knowledge is a dynamic process, which requires both time and sleep to be optimally consolidated.
sleep does not seem to be a critical factor for the formation of new cross-modal conceptual knowledge.
